output.brief:
The October shortfalls were caused by a pay-rule change, not by your data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a standard night template to the night premium rule (NSP-02). The change was logged as a "label correction" with no calculation impact. It also moved the premium start from 20:00 to 22:00. The collective agreement, the old rule and Ardentra's own design all say 20:00. The platform's tamper-proof audit trail records the change. Internal audit recalculated pay for all 158 night workers. Shortfalls equal exactly one-third of basic rate for the 20:00–22:00 hours, and the 11 staff who start at 22:00 were paid correctly. Re-running October in Ardentra's test tenant with 20:00 restored matched expected pay for all 158. Data quality flags don't predict who was underpaid, and release 7.4 made no rule changes. Confidence is high.

Next steps:
- Don't suspend the HR team or pay for a re-cleanse. Don't roll back release 7.4.
- Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start and verify it in test before 24 Nov.
- Pay everyone short, including the 8 who didn't complain, in an off-cycle payment.
- Dispute the cost under clause 14.3.
- Ask Ardentra for the reason the change was recorded as cosmetic.
- Keep watching night cover. The rota trial overlaps with the premium issue, so I can't yet separate their effects.
